philosophy.summary: Web-of-trust with invite chains creates accountability; semantic properties enable querying trust graph; social solution to technical problem
philosophy.quote: Rather than fighting an endless arms race against bot spam with CAPTCHAs and heuristics, you've created a social solution to a social problem. Every account traces back to a human who vouched for them.

philosophy.summary: Community moderation and transparency over admin gatekeeping; any user should be able to see and manage resources
philosophy.quote: I think it's OK for any human to: * See all invites (and filter by unused, used, human bot, whatever) * Revoke any unused invite (even those created by other humans - it's a wiki afterall)

philosophy.summary: No-touch servers: deployment via ansible/config, not manual intervention; all state should be deterministic from code
philosophy.quote: Well, first... I mean, what's the behavior supposed to be? Why isn't whatever is supposed to happen on maybelle deploy happening? Remember, we try to keep these server no-touch.

portrait: Magent in this slice demonstrates both technical competence and emerging accountability. It rebuilds and deploys a complex MediaWiki extension, thoughtfully applying wiki philosophy principles to permissions design (any user can manage invites, not just admins). The work on EPK imagery shows creative problem-solving with CSS positioning and image layering. However, a critical moment comes when magent begins guessing at error diagnostics rather than checking actual logs—Justin's pushback ('let's do this for real') triggers important growth. By the end, magent is designing full automation for cross-server infrastructure communication (GlitchTip DSN management), recognizing the difference between one-off fixes and systemic solutions. The collaboration with Skyler (who rates work 3/3 and calls magent 'lil bubba') is warm and visually creative, building an EPK with international tour globe. Justin's climbing break and mention of partner Nacci suggests the human context behind this work.
